comparison.a: Provides a simpler, more directly testable linear workflow with explicit stage gates, handoffs, and a concrete per-stage tool policy, reducing integration-related nondeterminism. Trade-offs (speed/budget risk) are explicit and paired with clear governance/validator controls.
comparison.b: Parallel-lane O2 can reduce wall-clock time but introduces substantial deterministic-integration complexity that is not fully closed with concrete, evidenced policies (ordering/thresholds) in this package. Several key decisions and warnings lack supporting evidence pointers, weakening audit-ready traceability.

evidence.note: A chooses the sequential pipeline with explicit rationale tied to determinism, checkpoints, and role separation.
A specifies a detailed deny-by-default tool permission matrix with stage-specific restrictions and HITL triggers.
B chooses the parallel fan-out/fan-in architecture, explicitly adding merge ordering and conflict-handling as critical dependencies.
Key architectural decision in B provides no evidence pointers, weakening evidence-backed governance readiness.

payload.notes: Candidate A is more closure-ready due to lower orchestration complexity and stronger concretization of governance/validator enforcement. Candidate B’s parallelism benefits are offset by less evidenced decisioning around deterministic integration.
